title: Five families, five signatures
caption: The chapter's organizing move: each architecture family answers the same three counts - weights stored, MACs performed, bytes resident - and the answer predicts which iron-law term saturates first. Note the transformer alone gets two cells: prefill and decode share weights but not regimes.

title: Prefill and decode regimes
caption: Why one model gets two rows in the workload profile. Prompt evaluation is a weight-reusing GEMM (compute-bound); each generated token is a GEMV that rereads every weight plus a KV cache growing ~307 KB per token - bandwidth-bound at ~1 FLOP/byte.

title: The embedding capacity wall
caption: Recommendation tables are feasibility problems before they are performance problems: a 51.2 GB table fits an 80 GB accelerator, two do not. The three escapes - shrink, move, partition - each relocate the cost rather than remove it.
